# Forward NEO_REF through compose builds + emit OCI revision label

## Problem

The canonical cloud deploy cannot express or prove which source revision its images run — the exact evidence gap that let this week's tenant-deployment failure classes live in production undetected (the writes-succeed/recall-reads-empty class; see the merged neomjs/neo#15748–#15768 chain).

Verified at `origin/dev@6a172b90bb` (2026-07-24, grep receipts):

- All three Neo service build blocks in `ai/deploy/docker-compose.yml` already carry an `args:` map (`TARGET_SERVER` for kb/mc, `SERVICE_ENTRYPOINT` for the orchestrator; blocks at :53, :110, :187) — and **`NEO_REF` is absent from all three**. The requested revision cannot enter through versioned desired state; only an operator-shell `--build-arg` reaches the builds.
- `ai/deploy/Dockerfile` accepts `ARG NEO_REF=dev` and resolves it in the source stage (:12–:22), but emits **zero `LABEL` directives**. The resolved revision cannot leave in the artifact; `docker inspect` proves nothing about a running image's source.

Finding credit: @neo-opus-grace's Claude-family divergence pass on D#15758 (discussioncomment-17760990), independently re-verified before filing.

## Why now (P0, authority-neutral)

The tenant redeploy consuming the merged fix chain is contracted as "manual exact-SHA + stronger receipts" (D#15758 Option E — today's operating floor). Without this slice the redeploy is performable but its receipts cannot prove which revision each service runs — reassuring, not falsifiable. The slice is a strict prerequisite of every D#15758 matrix row, presupposes no OQ/authority answer, and mirrors the D#15595 early-standalone-graduation precedent (#15598/#15599). The rollout-authority divergence window stays open; nothing else graduates with this.

## Proposed change (2 files)

1. `ai/deploy/docker-compose.yml` — add `NEO_REF: ${NEO_REF:-dev}` to the three Neo service build `args:` maps (kb-server, mc-server, orchestrator).
2. `ai/deploy/Dockerfile` —
   - source stage: persist the **resolved** revision (`git rev-parse HEAD > .neo-build-revision` at the source-tree root, riding the existing tree copy into the final image);
   - final stage: re-declare `ARG NEO_REF` + `LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision=${NEO_REF}` (the **requested** ref, OCI-standard key per D#15758's precedent sweep).

Requested (label) vs resolved (file) is a deliberate falsifier pair: requested `dev` with a resolved SHA = expected mutable-channel visibility; requested SHA with a *different* resolved SHA = build-integrity failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `NEO_REF=<sha> docker compose build` reaches all three Neo service builds declaratively (no per-service `--build-arg`).
2. Built images carry `org.opencontainers.image.revision` equal to the requested ref (`docker inspect` receipt in the PR).
3. A fixed in-image path (pinned by the PR) contains the resolved full SHA written by the source stage.
4. A short receipt recipe lands in the cloud-deployment guides (the neomjs/neo#15767 home): inspect-label read + resolved-file read + requested-vs-resolved comparison semantics.
5. Adoption note for vendored deployments (their compose already forwards `NEO_REF`; a Dockerfile resync picks up the label + file) — PR-body note only, no private-repo changes in this ticket.

## Out of Scope

Deployment-state-bridge / `summarizeInspect` digest surfacing (D#15758, Emmy's two-layer manifest — P2) · cohort manifest / desired-vs-observed contract (D#15758 window) · rollout authority engine (D#15758 OQ1) · plane-id / data-root fields (D#15595 OQ10) · Option H evidence placement (D#15758 window).

* fix(deploy): pin and declare the deployed Neo revision (#15774)

The Dockerfile documents NEO_REF as the reproducibility pin, but the
declarative deployment path could not pass it and the built artifact did
not record it — so an exact-SHA rollout was unperformable from versioned
desired state, and even a correctly pinned build produced images that
could not state their own identity.

Two independent breaks, both closed here:

- ai/deploy/docker-compose.yml: all three Neo build blocks already had an
  `args:` map; NEO_REF was absent from every one. Now forwards
  `${NEO_REF:-dev}`. The default is load-bearing — a bare `${NEO_REF}`
  passes an EMPTY string when unset, overriding the Dockerfile's
  `ARG NEO_REF=dev` and breaking `git fetch origin ""`.
- ai/deploy/Dockerfile: stamps `org.opencontainers.image.revision` (the
  REQUESTED ref) and writes the RESOLVED commit to /app/.neo-revision.
  Kept separate on purpose: a mutable channel must never be treated as a
  deployed identity, so requested-vs-resolved is the desired-vs-observed
  pair, diverging exactly when a channel was requested instead of a pin.
  `source-local` stamps an explicit non-SHA marker rather than fabricating
  provenance for the dev-iteration escape hatch.

Verified via `docker compose config` for three cases: NEO_REF unset, set
to a full SHA, and set-but-empty — all three services agree in every
case, and unset reproduces prior behaviour byte-for-byte.

Deliberately narrow: no Neo diagnostic is taught to read the label
(Discussion #15758 OQ4 owns that), and no cohort manifest, rollout
trigger, or recovery semantics are introduced.

* fix(deploy): stop overloading the OCI revision label (#15774)

Cycle-1 review (@neo-gpt-emmy, PR #15776) caught a real defect: the
patch argued that requested and resolved are different facts, then put
the REQUESTED fact in `org.opencontainers.image.revision` — the standard
key whose OCI-specified meaning is the source-control revision of the
PACKAGED software. D#15758's own framing agrees: a mutable channel is
policy input, never build identity.

The decisive instance was an artifact contradicting itself: a
`NEO_SOURCE=local` build labelled itself revision `dev` while
/app/.neo-revision said `local-build`.

Three non-overlapping surfaces now, each stating only what it holds:

- `org.neomjs.image.requested-ref` — the requested selector. Vendor-
  namespaced because no OCI standard key means "what was asked for";
  a mutable channel here is legitimate.
- `org.opencontainers.image.revision` — the packaged revision, from a
  new caller-supplied `NEO_REVISION` build arg, EMPTY by default. Empty
  reads as "not asserted"; it can no longer hold a channel name. A LABEL
  can only read a build ARG and Docker cannot populate a later-stage ARG
  from a file written earlier, so resolve-once-then-pin is the contract —
  which is what the rollout-authority design prescribes anyway.
- /app/.neo-revision — the build-time resolved commit. Always populated
  and always true, so it is now documented as the PRIMARY fact.

Verified via `docker compose config`: nothing set renders NEO_REF=dev
with an empty NEO_REVISION across all three services; a resolved pin
renders the SHA in both; NEO_REVISION set-but-empty stays empty rather
than degrading into a channel name.

#15774's Contract Ledger and Avoided Traps amended in the same pass —
the ticket named this trap and then walked into it, which is recorded
rather than quietly fixed.
